step1_analysis.description: This circuit is a double-balanced I/Q upconversion mixer based on a Gilbert cell architecture. It mixes differential baseband I and Q signals with quadrature LO signals to produce a modulated RF/IF output.

paper_reference.title: SiGe W-CDMA Transmitter for Mobile Terminal Application

power_consumption.description: Total DC power consumed by the mixer circuit.

sky130_expected.calculation: Assuming a bias current of ~2mA per branch (4 branches) from VBIAS=0.7V, total current is ~8mA. Power = 8mA * 1.8V = 14.4mW.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The paper's 270mW is for the entire transmitter IC. The mixer block alone in a 1.8V CMOS process will consume significantly less power.

conversion_gain.description: Voltage ratio of the IF output to the baseband input.

sky130_expected.calculation: Gain ≈ (2/π) * gm * Rload. With Rload = 500Ω and gm ≈ 10mS, Gain ≈ 3.18 V/V = 10 dB.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Typical upconversion mixers have a conversion gain around 5-15 dB depending on the load resistors and transconductance of the baseband differential pairs.

oip3.description: Third-order output intercept point, indicating linearity.

sky130_expected.calculation: Mixer OIP3 is typically 10-15 dB above the 1dB compression point. With 1.8V supply, max output swing is ~1Vpp.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The 25 dBm OIP3 reported in the paper is for the entire transmitter (including the PA driver). The mixer alone will have a lower OIP3, typically around 5-10 dBm in a 1.8V process.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench to measure power consumption and conversion gain of the I/Q upconversion mixer using a 1GHz LO and 10MHz baseband signal.
step3_testbench.spice:
* I/Q Upconversion Mixer Testbench
.lib "sky130_fd_pr/models/sky130.lib.spice" tt

* DUT (Adapted for standard SPICE syntax and SKY130)
R1 VCC IFON 500
R2 VCC IFOP 500
Q1 IFON LOIN N1_D npn
Q2 IFOP LOIP N1_D npn
Q5 IFON LOQN N2_D npn
Q6 IFOP LOQP N2_D npn
Q3 IFON LOQN N3_D npn
Q4 IFOP LOQP N3_D npn
Q7 IFON LOIN N4_D npn
Q8 IFOP LOIP N4_D npn
M1 N1_D BBIN N5 GND sky130_fd_pr__nmos5v W=20u L=0.5u
M3 N2_D BBQP N7 GND sky130_fd_pr__nmos5v W=20u L=0.5u
M2 N3_D BBIQ N6 GND sky130_fd_pr__nmos5v W=20u L=0.5u
M4 N4_D BBQN N8 GND sky130_fd_pr__nmos5v W=20u L=0.5u
M5 N5 VBIAS GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nmos5v W=40u L=0.5u
M6 N6 VBIAS GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nmos5v W=40u L=0.5u
M7 N7 VBIAS GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nmos5v W=40u L=0.5u
M8 N8 VBIAS GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nmos5v W=40u L=0.5u
R3 N5 N6 100
R4 N7 N8 100

* Generic NPN model for the BiCMOS switching quad
.model npn npn (bf=100 is=1e-16 vaf=50)

* DC Sources
VCC VCC 0 1.8
VVBIAS VBIAS 0 0.7

* LO signals (1 GHz, 0.6Vpp differential)
VLOIP LOIP 0 dc 1.2 sin(1.2 0.3 1G 0 0 0)
VLOIN LOIN 0 dc 1.2 sin(1.2 0.3 1G 0 0 180)
VLOQP LOQP 0 dc 1.2
VLOQN LOQN 0 dc 1.2

* BB signals (10 MHz, 0.2Vpp differential on I-channel)
VBBIN BBIN 0 dc 0.9 sin(0.9 0.1 10Meg 0 0 180)
VBBIQ BBIQ 0 dc 0.9 sin(0.9 0.1 10Meg 0 0 0)
VBBQP BBQP 0 dc 0.9
VBBQN BBQN 0 dc 0.9

.control
  * Run transient analysis for 2 baseband periods
  tran 10p 200n
  
  * 1. Measure Power Consumption
  let pwr = -i(VCC) * 1.8
  meas tran avg_pwr avg pwr
  
  * 2. Measure Conversion Gain
  * The output is a DSB-SC signal. The envelope varies at the baseband frequency.
  let vout_diff = v(IFOP) - v(IFON)
  meas tran vout_max max vout_diff from=100n to=200n
  meas tran vout_min min vout_diff from=100n to=200n
  
  * Calculate peak output voltage and gain
  let vout_pk = (vout_max - vout_min) / 2
  let vin_pk = 0.2
  let gain = vout_pk / vin_pk
  let gain_db = 20 * log10(gain)
  
  print avg_pwr
  print gain_db
  
  quit
.endc
.end
